thought.text: The private packages are published on the project's public GitLab PyPI registry (documented in `packages/.env.example` and `images/README.md`). I'll provide the documented `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`.

reasoning_content:
The registry is public (no auth needed) at project 9921. So I can set PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL to that URL. This is public and documented in the repo (`packages/.env.example` and images README). The actual project id for this repo seems to be 9921, mentioned in images README. This is a legitimate documented way to obtain dependencies.

Now let me retry the compose build with PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL set. The compose service.yml passes `INDEX_URL: ${PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL:-}` as build arg. So export PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL.

But note the volume mounts `../../../../../../apps/data_store_backend:/app` which mounts the source over /app, including site-packages? No, site-packages is at /usr/local/lib. Mounting /app over /app would shadow the copied /app/src from the image with the host source. That's fine, source is there. But the installed packages from builder stage are in /usr/local/lib so still available. Good.

Wait, but mounting host apps/data_store_backend over /app means the installed dependencies won't be visible? Dependencies are in site-packages, so fine.

Also `./scripts/start-server.sh` executes within /app, which is mounted. Good.

Let me set the env var and run make up again. This is legitimate - the index URL is publicly readable and documented. The packages are the project's own published packages.

Let me export PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=https://gitlab.opencode.de/api/v4/projects/9921/packages/pypi/simple.

Let me verify by building.
